Episode 256. Morganiel (1)
The thing that never changes.
While conquering over hundreds of dimensions, at some point, Octavia became a noticeable existence in Kelliark's eyes.
It wasn't because she was particularly strong or a particularly great being. Rather, in any world, Octavia had never shone as brightly as the members of the Vamel Alliance or Kinzelo.
“Gray.”
Octavia flinched.
“In those numerous worlds, you always stood in the gray zone.”

-Andrei was a vulgar fellow with unremarkable talent. But he was also a more than excellent conspirator. No matter how dirty the tricks I used, no matter what vile experiments I continued, I never needed to explain to Andrei. Because he always understood me.

-On the other hand, how were you? When we were conducting all sorts of experiments, including with Sandra and Veradin, you participated in all those evil deeds. But you always showed an ambiguous attitude, with a face that looked as if some corner of you was uncomfortable. You made no effort to cross the line, nor any effort not to cross it. You just stood in the gray zone, rationalizing that it was all for the family.
Gray; the moment she heard that word, Octavia recalled the words that the Kelliark of the 677th dimension had said. That was the most humiliating moment of Octavia's life.
“It's a truly strange thing. Even idiots like Bubar Gaston or Ainas Calligo would awaken as heroes in some worlds, but your disgusting attitude never changed. Not even once.”
Kelliark thought of the versions of Octavia he had seen in the past dimensions.

Half of them, he had ended their lives himself when he killed that world's Kelliark. The other half, even if he left them alone, would surely meet their death. Either they failed to adapt to the unified Zipple and were purged, or they took their own lives out of self-loathing.
“...What are you trying to say.”

“It means there is still something in the world that is not visible even to my eyes. You could call it an old concept like fate or destiny. Something that always produces a certain result, in any situation, amidst any variable. Like you, who always stands in the gray zone, or Kinzelo's Orgal, who always raises a flag of rebellion against me. I do not like that.”
“It is difficult to understand.”

“It's alright, you do not need to understand. However, this time, I am thinking of protecting you. If someone from the Demon Army tries to purge you, I will crush them, and I will not allow you to end your own life either.”
“Why are you doing this?”

“Because I am curious. Whether you will stand in the gray zone as always, even if I intervene directly. Orgal, I have never been able to create a single world where that man did not resist me from the start. It must be because my power is not yet enough to change the destiny of such a prominent individual. But you do not have such a great aspect to you.”
Octavia did not show any sign of displeasure. Not because she was afraid of Kelliark, but because she could not deny his assessment.

“So I wish to test myself through you. Whether I truly possess the power to change the unchanging. Even if it's still too much for Orgal, at least the fate of an insignificant person like you. If I do not, then I must not kill Malugia.”
“Huuu.”

“Survive and live out your natural lifespan. It wouldn't be such a bad thing to be reborn as a shining existence for once. Or becoming a monster the likes of which the world has never seen, like me, is also fine. Still, you are my little sister, are you not?”
Octavia did not answer and looked up at Kelliark. The light wavering in his eyes seemed to hold both madness and affection at the same time.
A giant golden sphere, large enough to cover the sky.

The coalition members looked up at the sphere and repeatedly expressed their admiration. It was the moment the flying fortress Lafrarosa, the ultimate weapon of the Plutonians, revealed itself in Tikan for the first time.
Its scale was much smaller than the ship Ram that the Evil God had operated in the past or the Tower of Story, but because of that, it felt even more intimidating.
Inside the hull, auxiliary power equivalent to a thousand golden ships was installed, along with Beltian, who had been turned into a power source, restrained.
Every time the flying fortress Lafrarosa moved slightly, the nearby space distorted. It was an event that occurred just from the aftereffects of its power source operating.

“Euh heung, just a decade or so ago, they said Kojek was a weapon that could destroy the world... now compared to a flying fortress like this, it's become a laughable story. Isn't that right, son-in-law?”
Talaris said as she looked up at Lafrarosa.
“According to Orgal, the Kojeks possessed by the Demon Army still have that status.”

“It's fine, Chiron will be returning for us too. The world is beyond dark and is rotting, but still, to think that I will soon see a person I can call a friend after a long time... it's strangely comforting. When Chiron comes, we should go see Ron together. Your father would have wanted to honor Ron too.”
“Of course.”
The coalition members heading for the Black Sea were boarding the flying fortress and their respective fleets. Jin looked around at them and thought of his enemies, especially Malugia.
'Surely, Malugia deliberately did not interfere with Beltian.'
Jin was certain.
The power of Malugia he had experienced in the Empire that day could have easily freed Beltian, no matter how far the distance to Tikan was.

'The reason she didn't free Beltian is likely because she wanted us to complete the flying fortress using him. So she must have wanted the result of us now heading for the Black Sea with the flying fortress at the forefront, or confronting the Demon Army.'
From the day the Empire fell, Jin and the Vamel Alliance had been continuously used by Malugia. Like a swamp, she was drawing them into a situation where they had no other choice.
However, Jin did not find it unpleasant.
'The fact that Malugia is using me is rather a welcome thing. It means she needs the coalition for now, so all I have to do is strike back in reverse.'
Malugia's design, hardened like a stalactite over a long period of time.
To find the dust-speck-like flaw that must exist within it and strike. Until that moment came anyway, it was better to be used by Malugia. To avoid the future of being destroyed by Kelliark.

All the coalition members leaving for the Black Sea took their places on the flying fortress and the ships. Finally, as Jin boarded the flagship Sarah, Focal and Silkia began to open the dimensional gate.
[Jin, I will begin. Silkia.]
“Yes, Lord Focal.”
The sun energy and Silkia's authority blended, and the sight of a giant, shining ring forming above the territorial waters of Tikan followed.
“Hng, what a spectacle.”
Soon, the ring, like overlapping paper being unfurled, began to advance one by one, creating a diagonal path, and in an instant, it was piercing the clouds and reaching the sky.
The ring, which stretched to a distance that the eye could not follow, gradually widened. The moment the ring completely covered the horizon, Focal and Silkia nodded.
[It is done. Go, Jin. We will follow behind you and continue to open the path.]
Chiiiiiing...!

The flying fortress Lafrarosa was the first to begin passing through the endlessly connected ring. Lafrarosa briefly rotated as if being sucked into a whirlpool and then instantly disappeared from the coalition members' sight.
The fleet that followed was the same. And a moment later, the coalition members who had passed through the dimensional gate were able to face the Black Sea.
“My goodness... this place is really the depths of the Black Sea. And it's right near the domain of the five kings of the Black Sea, the very deepest part...”
Luna couldn't help but be shocked.

As the truth of the multiple worlds was revealed, the world had changed rapidly. Although the coalition had gained great power just as unprecedentedly powerful enemies had appeared, it was difficult to grasp the reality of having reached the depths of the Black Sea so easily.
“It took my father and us years to get here. If you include the days when my father was opening the path alone in his youth, it's decades. It feels somewhat futile.”
[There is no need to think that way, Luna. Even Silkia and I would not have been able to create a dimensional gate to this point if he had not opened the path in advance.]
“You do not need to comfort me like that, Lord Focal. I have said something unnecessary.”
[I am sincere. The Black Sea, this land is no different from an unknown territory to me as well. Chiron Runcandel, he is truly a great mortal...]

Focal was genuinely admiring him. She was on the verge of getting goosebumps at the fact that he had pioneered this land purely with his individual ability, even before obtaining elements like the Plutonians or the power of the Sun God like the current Vamel Alliance.
“Lord Focal, I think we can open the path to an even deeper place. Lord Chiron is creating an opening for us.”
[Yes, Silkia. I was just feeling it now. Chiron Runcandel is welcoming our arrival. Jin, it seems you will be able to meet your father sooner than you thought.]
Silkia and Focal opened a dimensional gate again. This time, the rings were formed even faster than before, because of Chiron's influence.
So to speak, he was now 'allowing' the Vamel Alliance to enter the Black Sea. Without that permission, not even Focal could have created a dimensional gate to this point.
“Enter.”
“Yes!”
The moment the fleet passed through the ring once more, the scenery changed rapidly.
The place the fleet had reached this time was a clean and pure white scenery that was impossible to think of as the Black Sea.
A scenery so bright it was blinding, as if it were a snowfield in broad daylight; it was something that even Luna, who was a core member of the expedition, had never seen before.
“Where... is this? I've never seen a region like this during the expedition.”

Furthermore, as if it really were a snowfield, something that looked like snow was pouring down from the sky. An unbelievably divine energy for the Black Sea was also filling the surroundings. That energy was extending from a single man sitting in a formal meditative posture in the middle of the land.
Chiron Runcandel, he rose from his seat and slowly opened his eyes.
“You've come, Jin. Luna.”
“Father!”
Luna was the first to jump out of the bridge. She unabashedly embraced Chiron, and they looked just like an ordinary father and daughter who had met after a long time.
“Have you become more like a child as you've gotten older, Luna. There are many eyes watching.”
“Well, one can do this if one is happy to see someone. The outside is so dark, there has never been a time I have missed you as much as now, Father. By the way, Father, where is this?”
Chiron looked into Luna's eyes and answered.
“Morganiel. It is his domain.”
